events.continuity_hook: Resolves the late Cleveland schedule change from the prior session before Maya travels.
events.interaction_goal: Finalize the Cleveland return-flight change and update the departure timing, seat choice, and receipt checklist.
events.scenario_brief: Maya receives approval to pay the fare difference for the Cleveland return change after the client moves Thursday’s closeout to 4:00 p.m. The later nonstop gives her more time to leave the hospital campus, retrieve her stored luggage if needed, and reach the airport without rushing, though it gets her back to Atlanta later in the evening. The original rear window seat cannot be carried over automatically, but the new flight still has one rear window and several aisle seats available. Remaining items are completing the airline change, selecting the best available seat, updating the calendar, and saving the new receipt for the trip file.

events.continuity_hook: Starts the next work-travel episode after the Cleveland trip is wrapped up.
events.interaction_goal: Frame the Minneapolis trip, identify workable flight windows and hotel areas, and list the client details needed before Maya requests approval.
events.scenario_brief: After returning from Cleveland, Maya gets a September request for an onsite training and workflow review with a Minneapolis client. The rough plan is to fly from Atlanta on Monday, run sessions Tuesday and Wednesday, and return Thursday after a possible client debrief. Atlanta to Minneapolis has several nonstop options, while one-stop itineraries save little and add travel risk. The main uncertainty is whether the work will be at the downtown office near the medical center or at a suburban training site, which will determine whether a downtown hotel, suburban hotel, or airport-area hotel makes sense. Remaining items are the exact site address, Tuesday start time, Thursday end time, nightly hotel ceiling, and whether a coworker needs to coordinate arrival timing.

events.continuity_hook: Continues Minneapolis planning once the worksite and meeting times are confirmed.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the main Minneapolis flight-and-hotel combinations and choose the practical approval-ready plan.
events.scenario_brief: The Minneapolis client confirms that the sessions will be at the downtown medical center office, with an 8:30 a.m. Tuesday start, a full Wednesday schedule, and a Thursday debrief expected to end around noon. The cleanest outbound is a Monday late-morning nonstop that lands with enough time for hotel check-in and prep. For Thursday, an early-afternoon nonstop is possible but tight if the debrief runs long, while a late-afternoon nonstop leaves a calmer margin. Hotel choices include a downtown property close to the office with strong guest ratings, on-site dining, and paid breakfast; a suite-style hotel with included breakfast but a longer walk or short rideshare; and a cheaper airport-area property that would make both client mornings less predictable.

events.continuity_hook: Moves the Minneapolis work trip from comparison into booking while the approved flights and hotel are still available.
events.interaction_goal: Finalize the Minneapolis flights, hotel, seat choices, room request, local transportation notes, and confirmation records.
events.scenario_brief: Maya’s manager approves the Monday late-morning nonstop to Minneapolis, the Thursday late-afternoon nonstop home, and the downtown hotel as long as the room remains cancellable. The fare and hotel rate are still available, and the hotel confirms a quiet-room request can be added but not guaranteed. Breakfast is not included, though there is an early cafe in the lobby and several casual dinner options within walking distance. Seat maps show rear window seats open on both flights, with forward seats mostly aisle or middle. Remaining items are completing the booking, selecting seats, adding the room request, noting airport-to-hotel transportation, and saving confirmations for reimbursement.

events.continuity_hook: Starts a new family leisure episode after the September work trip planning is handled.
events.interaction_goal: Frame the D.C. family weekend, compare airport and hotel-area tradeoffs, and identify what Maya needs to confirm with her spouse.
events.scenario_brief: With the school fall-break calendar settled, Maya starts exploring a three-night family museum weekend in Washington, D.C. with her spouse and child. They are considering a Friday departure and Monday return, hoping to arrive early enough for an easy first evening and return before Monday night gets too late. Nonstops from Atlanta to Reagan National are the most convenient for the city, while Dulles and Baltimore options sometimes price lower but add longer ground transfers. Hotel areas under consideration include Penn Quarter, Capitol Hill, Dupont Circle, and Arlington near Metro. The family wants easy access to Smithsonian museums, casual dinners, and enough room comfort for three people, while weighing included breakfast against being closer to the first two sightseeing days. Remaining items are exact dates, nightly budget, how much Metro walking feels reasonable, and whether any timed museum or monument plans should drive the hotel area.

events.continuity_hook: Continues the D.C. family weekend after the dates and airport priorities are clarified.
events.interaction_goal: Narrow the D.C. flights and hotel choice to one family-ready plan with the main tradeoffs clearly summarized.
events.scenario_brief: Maya’s spouse confirms the Friday-to-Monday fall-break window and wants the simplest city access over chasing the lowest fare. The leading flight plan is a late-morning nonstop from Atlanta to Reagan National and an early-afternoon nonstop home, while cheaper Dulles and Baltimore itineraries add transfer time and make the first or last day less smooth. The hotel shortlist has narrowed to a Penn Quarter hotel with strong ratings, walkable museum access, and many restaurants nearby but paid breakfast; a Capitol Hill suite-style option with included breakfast and more space but fewer nearby dinner choices; and an Arlington hotel with a lower nightly rate and larger rooms but Metro rides for most sightseeing. Remaining decisions are whether downtown convenience outweighs breakfast and room size, whether the Reagan fare is worth booking now, and whether to hold a cancellable hotel while they finalize museum plans.
